stages.title: SUBORDINATE ENRICHMENT — ONLY AFTER THE COMPLETE CORE

pills.text: CHANDRA DEFENDS THE NEHRUVIAN DEVELOPMENT MODEL AS A RATIONAL
SELF-RELIANCE, IMPORT SUBSTITUTION, A PUBLIC-SECTOR CORE, AND GROWTH WITH
ITS STRUCTURAL FLAW WAS THE LICENCE-PERMIT-QUOTA RAJ
RESERVATION) THAT PROTECTED INEFFICIENCY, THROTTLED SCALE AND COMPETITION, AND
THE 1991 REFORMS ARE PRESENTED NOT AS SURRENDER BUT
— RETAINING THE GOALS OF GROWTH, SELF-RELIANCE AND POVERTY

groups.heading: OPTIONAL SOURCE DEPTH
items: Chandra defends the Nehruvian development model as a rational choice for a poor economy —
self-reliance, import substitution, a public-sector core, and growth with equity within a democratic frame .
CAUTION: Its structural flaw was the licence-permit-quota raj : controls (IDRA 1951, MRTP, small-scale
reservation) that protected inefficiency, throttled scale and competition, and eroded productivity by the 1980s.

groups.heading: ADVANCED DEBATE
items: The 1991 reforms are presented not as surrender but as a corrective to excessive dirigisme
— retaining the goals of growth, self-reliance and poverty removal while changing the instruments.
CAUTION: The deeper argument: democracy shaped development — a free press helped avert famines, and popular
sovereignty prevented the coercive extraction of surplus from peasants and workers seen in authoritarian industrialisers.

groups.heading: LEGACY / NUANCE
items: Land reform : zamindari abolition (backed by the 1st and 4th Amendments) made about 20 million superior tenants owners.
The rough fall in tenancy area from 42% to 20–25% cannot be read simply as success because oral
Tenancy/ceiling implementation suffered from "personal cultivation" loopholes, benami transfers, poor records, delay and official collusion
Bhoodan/Gramdan could not substitute for structural reform.
